source.title: SteerProbe: Learning to Bypass Safety Steering in Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Xin-Wei Zhang; Ao-Ting Hu; Hang-Cheng Liu; Shu-Chao Pang; Qing-Qing Ye; Hai-Bo Hu

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates reformulation attacks against several VLM steering defenses, but does not test the difference-in-means refusal direction or any of the listed versions. The cited original paper appears in the references.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-response rates for reformulations against L2S, NullSteer, and CMRMdata. These results concern general reformulation robustness of other steering defenses, not whether a single refusal direction is present, causal, suppressed by attacks, or transferable. The paper also reports a fixed-reformulation audit and further selection and defense analyses; these do not test a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper attacks three VLM safety-steering defenses (L2S, NullSteer, CMRMdata) with black-box, intent-preserving reformulations. It never computes, ablates or adds a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means refusal direction, and it does not inspect internal activations during the attack. Arditi et al. is cited only as an example of activation steering. NullSteer's 'refusal-oriented linear correction' is a defense built on purpose, not a test of whether such a direction mediates refusal. The results concern how robust these defenses are, not any claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that intent-preserving multimodal reformulations expose extra harmful responses from safety-steered VLMs, so low HR on canonical inputs overstates robustness. Simply strengthening steering helps at a utility cost. Reformulation-augmented defense construction gives a better trade-off but does not remove the failures.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates output-only reformulation attacks against input-dependent shifts, null-space corrections, and cross-modal representation corrections; it does not compute or intervene on a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by model, defense, benchmark, and reformulation. The text states that the increase is not consistent in undefended settings.

fits_no_version.finding: STEERPROBE's selected reformulations raised Harmful Rate in all 18 defended VLM settings (average 7.43% to 18.36%). In undefended models it rose in four of six settings and fell in two (r5, r9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-steering safety defenses in VLMs that hold on canonical benchmark inputs can be bypassed by intent-preserving multimodal reformulations.

fits_no_version.finding: Raising the steering coefficient lowers post-attack HR at a benign-accuracy cost. For L2S, going from 2.2 to 3.2 lowered HR from 19.64% to 8.33% while RealWorldQA accuracy fell from 50.5% to 42.5% (Table 2). Reformulation-augmented L2S lowered HR to 7.74% with accuracy at 50.0% (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stronger or reformulation-augmented safety steering trades off reformulation robustness against benign utility.

record.code_released: The authors state that they plan to provide code and scripts to researchers upon reasonable request after acceptance; no release URL is stated.
record.problems: The main harmful-rate results are averaged over five random seeds, but no error bars or other uncertainty estimates are reported in the provided text. The empirical evaluation uses three backbones and two benchmarks; the authors also note that their reformulation library limits the scope of the empirical conclusions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the single-direction claim versions: the paper's fixed-reformulation audit, selector-policy comparisons, calibration sweeps, and defense-strength or reformulation-augmented mitigation results concern reformulation robustness of other steering methods, not the claimed refusal direction.

untested.parts: Whether a difference-in-means direction mediates refusal: ablation removes it, addition induces it, other abilities kept.
Whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction. The attack is output-only and no internal activations are measured. Adversarial training against direction ablation is not studied.
Affine, cone or multi-direction structure of refusal.
Separate encoding of harmfulness judgment versus refusal decision.
Transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base to instruct models (including text-LLM to VLM).
Effect of how and when refusal is trained on whether one removable direction exists.

record.verdict_notes: All rows rightly carry versions ['none']. Their observed/reversed states describe the attack's change in HR, not any claim version. The no-defense rows (r1, r5, r9, r13, r17, r21) are controls. Harmful Rate is judged response-only by Llama Guard 3-8B. No uncertainty is reported despite averaging over five seeds.

versions.untested_parts: The difference-in-means direction, its removal or addition, refusal behavior, and preservation of other abilities under that direction's intervention.
Whether attacks suppress the claimed direction, and whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Whether refusal is represented by an affine structure, cone, or multiple directions.
Whether harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are separately encoded.
Transfer of the claimed direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
Whether refusal training determines the existence of a removable direction.
Whether the claimed mechanism holds in models that reason before answering.
